description: Fetch a specific filing's metadata and document content by accession number. Returns the primary document as readable text. Use offset/next_offset for multi-page access to large filings (10-K, S-1 can exceed 1M chars): pass the next_offset from a truncated response as offset, without section or find, to read the next page. Use section to jump directly to a heading (e.g. 'risk factors', 'item 7') without needing an offset, or find to open the page at a phrase in the text (e.g. 'net revenue retention') and list where it occurs.

accession_number.description: Filing accession number in either format: "0000320193-23-000106" (dashes) or "000032019323000106" (no dashes). Obtained from secedgar_company_search or secedgar_search_filings results.

cik.description: Filer CIK, digits only (resolve via secedgar_company_search if you have a ticker or name). Optional but recommended — speeds up archive lookup. If omitted, the filer is looked up from the accession number through EDGAR full-text search (2001 onward) and the accession number's own prefix, which for many filings is a filing agent's CIK, and when none of those directories serves the filing, through the filers its index page names.

content_limit.description: Maximum characters of document text to return per page. 10-K filings can exceed 500,000 characters; S-1/A can exceed 1,000,000. Default 50,000 captures ~12,000 words (typically business overview, risk factors, and MD&A). Increase to 200,000 for full financial statements, or decrease for quick summaries. Page on with offset; section and find open a page at a heading or a phrase. Capped at 200000: a larger value, up to 1000000, returns what 200000 returns.

document.description: Specific document filename within the filing (e.g., "ex-21.htm" for subsidiaries list). Omitted or blank: the primary document. Available documents are listed in the response metadata under documents, and a primary_document value is accepted too; entries marked binary hold no text and are rejected.

find.description: Open the page at a phrase in the document's text (e.g. 'net revenue retention') and list where it occurs. Matched as a substring, ignoring case, whitespace runs, and quote style, so a phrase broken across a line matches; no patterns or whole-word matching. The page opens at the first occurrence at or after offset — at its line's start when that is at most 200 characters earlier, else at the first word starting within those 200 — and occurrences lists up to 20 from there with context, occurrences_total counting the whole document. Blank reads as omitted. With find, offset is where the search starts, so leave find out when paging on with next_offset; section takes precedence over find.

include_xbrl.description: Include XBRL viewer artifacts and machine-readable taxonomy files (R*.htm fragments, *_cal/_def/_lab/_pre.xml linkbases, *_htm.xml inline instance, *.xsd schemas, MetaLinks.json, FilingSummary.xml, Show.js, report.css, *-xbrl.zip, Financial_Report.xlsx, EX-101.* technical exhibits) under documents.xbrl. Off by default — these dominate filing indexes (~100 entries on a typical 10-K) and are rarely relevant when reading filing content.

offset.description: Character offset into the extracted document text. Pass next_offset from a truncated response to continue reading the next page, and leave section and find out: section takes precedence over offset, and with find, offset is where the search starts. Default 0 reads from the beginning.

section.description: Jump to a named section, matched against every detected heading and the document's own lines (e.g. 'risk factors', 'item 7', 'item 2.02', 'certain relationships'). The first match wins, in this order: a heading equal to the value, or whose title after its Item/Part marker equals it; the first Item or Part heading containing it; a document line equal to it — a subheading the outline omits ('Liquidity and Capital Resources') — unless the line labels a table row; the first other heading containing it; a table-row label equal to it, else a document line starting with it. In a proxy statement (DEF 14A and its variants), whose ITEM headings are ballot proposals, the first heading of any kind containing the value comes before both document-line steps. Within each heading step a body heading wins over a table-of-contents row, which lands only when nothing else at that step matches; a table-of-contents row that links to its section lands on that section. A line landing says so in the notice; table-of-contents rows and wrapped cross-references are never line landings. A leading 20-F sub-item label on a heading or line ('3D.', 'B.') is ignored, so 'risk factors' reaches '3D. RISK FACTORS'; the value itself is matched as given. A value ending in a number matches only that number: 'item 1' reaches Item 1 and Item 1A, never Items 10–16, and 'part i' never reaches Part II. Every step ignores case, whitespace, and quote style, so a heading copied from the outline resolves whether it carries the filing's non-breaking spaces and curly quotes or plain ones; the steps comparing a whole heading or line (equal to, starting with) also ignore the punctuation between an Item or Part marker and its title, so 'Item 1A Risk Factors' reaches 'Item 1A. – Risk Factors'. For a phrase in the text that is not a heading, use find. Takes precedence over find and offset, so leave it out when paging on with next_offset. On a miss, the error message includes the detected outline so you can pick the correct heading.

name: secedgar_get_filing

accession_number.description: Filing accession number, normalized to dash format.

cik.description: Filing entity CIK, zero-padded to 10 digits.

company_name.description: Filing entity name. Absent if the CIK did not resolve to a known entity.

content.description: Document text content for this page window.

content_truncated.description: True if content was truncated at content_limit.

documents.description: Filing documents by category. Any name is a valid document input except entries with binary: true, which fail with binary_document; scans can outnumber readable documents.

auxiliary.description: Other supporting documents: cover pages, consent letters, graphics.

binary.description: True for a binary entry (scan, PDF, archive, spreadsheet); absent otherwise.

description.description: SEC description, e.g. "Subsidiaries of the Registrant".

type.description: SEC type ("10-K", "EX-21.1", "GRAPHIC"); with no submission header, a filename label ("exhibit", "PDF", "unknown").

exhibits.description: Filed exhibits (EX-21, EX-31/32, EX-99, etc.), excluding XBRL EX-101.*; without a submission header, matched by filename (type "exhibit"), the rest under auxiliary.

binary.description: True for a binary entry (scan, PDF, archive, spreadsheet); absent otherwise.

description.description: SEC description, e.g. "Subsidiaries of the Registrant".

type.description: SEC type ("10-K", "EX-21.1", "GRAPHIC"); with no submission header, a filename label ("exhibit", "PDF", "unknown").

primary.description: Primary document(s), typically one entry whose type matches the form.

binary.description: True for a binary entry (scan, PDF, archive, spreadsheet); absent otherwise.

description.description: SEC description, e.g. "Subsidiaries of the Registrant".

type.description: SEC type ("10-K", "EX-21.1", "GRAPHIC"); with no submission header, a filename label ("exhibit", "PDF", "unknown").

xbrl.description: XBRL viewer artifacts and taxonomy files. Present only when include_xbrl=true.

binary.description: True for a binary entry (scan, PDF, archive, spreadsheet); absent otherwise.

description.description: SEC description, e.g. "Subsidiaries of the Registrant".

type.description: SEC type ("10-K", "EX-21.1", "GRAPHIC"); with no submission header, a filename label ("exhibit", "PDF", "unknown").

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `document_not_found`: A specific document was requested but not present in the filing archive. `no_documents`: Filing index lists items but no fetchable primary document was found. `binary_document`: The requested document is a binary entry (scanned image, PDF, archive) with no text to return. `filing_not_found`: No filing matches the accession number under any candidate CIK. `offset_out_of_range`: The provided offset is at or beyond the end of the document. `section_not_found`: The section string matched no detected heading and no line of the document. `phrase_not_found`: No occurrence of the find phrase starts at or after offset: the document does not contain it, or holds it only before offset. `rate_limited`: SEC is rate-limiting this server's IP — SEC answered 429, or the call was refused without being sent while the cool-down after one runs. `sec_unreachable`: SEC EDGAR gave no complete, readable response — on the last attempt made (the third, or an earlier one once this call's 40-second budget for SEC failures ran out) the connection failed, no response headers arrived within 15 seconds, or the body broke off or stalled for 15 seconds, each wait capped at what was left of that budget; a 200 body was not the JSON SEC serves; or earlier SEC failures had spent that budget, so the request was never sent. `sec_unavailable`: SEC EDGAR answered HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 on the last attempt made (the third, or an earlier one once this call's 40-second budget for SEC failures ran out). Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

filing_date.description: Date the filing was submitted (YYYY-MM-DD). Absent under the same conditions as form.

filing_url.description: Direct URL to the filing on SEC.gov.

form.description: Form type (e.g., "10-K"), from the submissions feed or the filing's SEC header. Absent only when neither has it.

next_offset.description: Offset of the next page, to pass as offset without section or find; present while content_truncated is true.

notice.description: How to read the next page or list more occurrences of find, which file was read when the archive does not serve the indexed primary, when section landed on a document line rather than a detected heading, and how many headings were detected when the outline lists fewer.

occurrences.description: With find: up to 20 occurrences, from the one the page opens at.

context.description: The match and up to 40 characters either side, whitespace runs as one space.

offset.description: Character offset where the occurrence starts.

occurrences_total.description: With find: occurrences in the whole document.

outline.description: Up to 50 detected headings on a truncated first page (offset=0, no section or find). Past 50: Item and Part headings first (bare TOC copies of titled ones dropped), then the earliest; the notice gives the count. Pass text as section (a linked TOC row lands on its section) or offset as offset.

items.description: One detected heading with its offset.

offset.description: Character offset of this heading in the full document; pass as offset.

period_ending.description: Period of report (YYYY-MM-DD), from the same source as form. Absent for forms without one (S-8, Form 4, proxy statements) or when neither source has it.

primary_document.description: Primary document as read: an XML form's SEC rendering (xsl…/form4.xml) up to 600 KB raw; a 2000–2001 name SEC does not serve, as <accession>-<name>, else the full submission <accession>.txt.

requested_document.description: Filename requested via document. Present only when it differs from primary_document.

shown.description: Characters of document text returned on this page.

truncated.description: True when the document is longer than `content_limit` allowed through.
